findings.reason: one edge (s15 depends on s5) or one sentence in §15 prevents a node from implementing the fallback against a narrower notion of a named route than §5 relies on.
findings.text: §5 makes "a route set by `crew queue edit`" a named route that "§15's fallback never moves", but the plan's `plan-section-depends-on` gives s15 only s4, s7 and s8, so a node implementing §15 from its own text would treat only `--local`, `--backend` and `--model` as dispatcher-named and would fall back a route the coordinator set by edit.

findings.reason: the cycle refusal is the section's only protection against a deadlocked queue, and as written the node will either invent an undeclared batch API or drop the guard, leaving it unproved.
findings.text: §8's arm "a test queues three requests whose `--after` refs form a cycle, and the batch is refused naming all three, with nothing stored" cannot be built as written: `--after <request-id>` must name an existing request (the same section refuses "a wait that names ... a request that does not exist"), a request id is the run id a dispatch assigns at queue time, and no batch queue surface is declared, so three new requests cannot reference one another in one batch.

findings.reason: an implementer must import a private helper or invent a second landed predicate, which is exactly the drift §8 closes for manifest statuses by naming one vocabulary.
findings.text: §8 requires "landing, not promotion of an unreviewed head, ... satisfies a wait" and "Even a `complete` manifest satisfies a wait only once its run has landed", yet it names no reader of a run's landed state; the only reader in the tree is the private `_promoted_run_ids` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:550`), which is not in §8's write paths.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every file and symbol §5 and §8 cite resolves in the tree: `_launch_queued` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:158`), `_node_from_pointer` (`:106`), `_store_brief` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2241`), `_brief_digest` (`:2204`), `parse_manifest` (`reckon/crew/reports.py:317`), `TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES` (`:126`), `parse_plan_ref` (`reckon/_schema.py:276`), `--brief` (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1088`), `TaskNode` (`reckon/crew/node.py:724`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's cycle arm ("queues three requests whose `--after` refs form a cycle, and the batch is refused") cannot be constructed from the `--after` surface §8 itself declares.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5's logs are declared under the run directory and both sections' write paths are repository paths plus a new test file; nothing lands in a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — neither section carries a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into a symbol, a file or a comment, and neither writes changelog prose; `steering.md` and `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` are mechanism names.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8 makes a wait resolve only once the upstream run "has landed" but names no reader of landed state, so the section's own vocabulary rule is not carried through to the landing predicate.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable (the launch-time steering file and the verbs that edit it), and §8 carries one (the cross-plan DAG wait); §5's `reprioritise` takes its semantics from §4 and its `drop` takes over `crew discard`'s existing behaviour.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5 defines a route set by `crew queue edit` as a "named route" that "§15's fallback never moves", but `plan-section-depends-on` (snapshot line 22) gives s15 the edges s4, s7 and s8 and none to s5, so §15 can be dispatched without the definition it consumes.
